readiness.primary_reason: Case includes explicit states, target/decoy entities, node regions, hotspot spans, typed objectives, and confidence/clash guardrails; wet-lab construct details can further tighten thresholds.

design_goal.primary: Design a CaM/EF-hand-like switch where calcium-loaded state binds MLCK-like peptide better than apo state.
design_goal.formal_success_definition: Improve the typed positive-state objectives while suppressing typed negative/decoy objectives, preserving local node confidence, and avoiding severe clashes or unfolding.

positive_signals: EF-hand loops preserve acidic/polar calcium pocket chemistry.
failure_signals: Peptide binds equally in apo state.
Switch arises from unfolding or clashes.

benchmark_start.rationale: Native calmodulin is already a calcium-gated peptide binder; the executable start neutralizes EF-hand loop chemistry so recovery of calcium/peptide behavior is measurable.
benchmark_start.interpretation: The executable binder segments are intentionally degraded relative to the reference/oracle sequence so evolution has measurable room to improve. The reference sequence is metadata only and is not used as the starting template.

information_gaps: Exact target peptide or protein readout for the calcium sensor.
Allowed edits in EF-loop acidic residues versus scaffold helices.
Whether the goal is calcium affinity tuning, peptide affinity switching, or both.
